title: Sen. Boozman and Rep. Carol Miller Disclosed Small Stock Sales: Aptiv and Honeywell Aerospace
content:
Sen. John Boozman (AR) disclosed a $1,001–$15,000 sale of Aptiv (APTV) stock on October 21, 2026, and Rep. Carol Devine Miller (WV-1) disclosed a $710.52 sale of Honeywell Aerospace (HONA) stock on October 30, 2026. Both were single-trade filings.

Trade data: Bargo, compiled from U.S. House and Senate STOCK Act filings.

Sep 25APTVAptiv PLC Ordinary SharesSale, $1,001–$15,000$44.79 vs. $41.34 (−7.70%)
Sep 29HONAHoneywell Aerospace Inc.Sale, $710.52 (exact amount)$155.44 vs. $157.50 (+1.33%)

Boozman: transaction Sep 25, 2026, disclosed Oct 21 (26 days later), Senate. Miller: transaction Sep 29, 2026, disclosed Oct 30 (31 days later), House.

What's been disclosed

  • Sen. John Boozman (AR): one sale of Aptiv PLC (APTV), $1,001–$15,000, on September 25. Bargo's estimate puts Aptiv about 7.7% lower on November 3 than on the sale date.
  • Rep. Carol Devine Miller (WV-1): one sale of Honeywell Aerospace (HONA), $710.52 (an exact amount, not a band), on September 29. Bargo's estimate puts the stock about 1.3% higher on November 3.
  • Scale: both are small filings, and neither says anything about the member's wider holdings.

Quick FAQ

How long after the trades were they disclosed?
26 days after the Aptiv sale and 31 days after the Honeywell Aerospace sale. The STOCK Act gives members 45 days from the transaction to disclose it.

Why are the amounts ranges?
Filings report value bands such as $15,001–$50,000 instead of exact dollar amounts.

Where does the price comparison come from?
It is Bargo's estimate, comparing the price on the transaction date with the November 3 price. It is not the member's actual execution price.
